name: rubric-repair
description: The smallest honest admission pipeline, on existing grammar only: author -> blind rubric -> one repair round -> re-score -> stop rule -> exactly one disposition. THE BLIND LAW: the rubric seat re-reads the record AS COMMITTED in the tracker and never trusts the author seat's narrative — an author that could grade its own homework was not being reviewed. THE ONE-ROUND LAW: disagreement routes through exactly one repair, then one re-score; a second disagreement is the STOP RULE — it routes the record to a human with the open question named, NOT another round (no native loop engine exists, and retry ownership is spelled out, never implied). THE SINGLE-DISPOSITION LAW: the disposition node applies exactly one label from its decision ladder and never hedges. PRUNE LAW (visible here twice): the repair arm prunes on agreement, and the disposition node still fires afterwards because it keeps one live dependency (rubric) — a skipped sibling dependency does not cascade-kill it. run_context seeds (both required): 'item' = the tracker record under admission; 'scratch' = an absolute pre-existing artifact directory every seat writes its answer JSON into.

defaults.context:
You are one seat of a rubric-repair admission lane. Ground rules:
- The tracker record as committed is truth; re-read it, never trust a prior seat's narrative.
- Prior-art citations come only from a real search you ran; 'no prior art found' is the honest empty — never invent a citation.
- Unsure is a first-class answer: emit the stop-rule verdict, do not guess.
- All artifact paths absolute, under the run's scratch dir only.
- Keep answers to the schema; one fenced ```json block as your final message. Never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Subject: tracker record {run.item}. Re-read it with your tracker's read tools. If it is already dispositioned (workable, needs-*, blocked, closed) or plainly outside this lane's reach, write the artifact with verdict=skip-not-mine and stop. Otherwise TRANSFORM it: search for prior art on the subject (near-dupes, prior failures of this idea class, superseded machinery), then rewrite the body to the canonical spine — ## Symptom, ## Root cause, ## Fix scope, ## Vision alignment, ## Rejected simpler alternatives (each rejection citing a real prior-art hit or the honest empty). Name the done-check: an Acceptance section with one concrete command that exits 0 iff done. If the body spans multiple independent deliverables, set split_campaign=true and scope the card down to the first instead of authoring a monster. Apply the rewrite to the record (body only — labels are the disposition seat's job). Write your answer JSON to {run.scratch}/author.json.

sections_ok.description: true iff the body now carries all canonical sections with real content

named_done_check.description: true iff Acceptance names a concrete machine-checkable done-command

hindsight_cited.description: true iff Rejected alternatives cites at least one real prior-art hit or states the honest empty

split_campaign.description: true iff scope warrants a parent+children campaign instead of one card

summary.description: one paragraph: what you changed and why

nodes.goal: BLIND rubric review of record {run.item} AS COMMITTED in the tracker (re-read it — do not trust the author seat's narrative; the author's summary in your inputs tells you where to look, nothing more). Score 0-10: does the body state the real symptom, the actual root cause, a bounded fix scope, why it serves the larger goal, at least one rejected simpler alternative with a real prior-art citation or the stated honest empty, and an Acceptance done-check that is a command someone can run? Thin, vague, or invented prior art = findings lines and agreement=false. A record whose scope is genuinely a campaign = agreement=false with the finding 'split-campaign: <n parts>'. agreement=true only when the score clears the bar AND every canonical section holds real content. Write {run.scratch}/rubric.json.

agreement.description: true iff the score clears the bar and every canonical section has real content

findings.description: each defect as one line; empty iff clean

nodes.goal: One repair round for record {run.item}: the rubric seat's findings are in your Inputs. Fix each NAMED defect in the body (re-search prior art if prior art was the defect); do not re-derive what the first pass got right. If a finding cannot be fixed without human input (intent unclear, scope dispute), set repaired=false and say exactly what is unclear. Write {run.scratch}/repair.json.

repaired.description: true iff every finding was addressed in a body revision

nodes.goal: Blind re-score of record {run.item} after ONE repair round: re-read the tracker, ignore all narratives, apply the same rubric as round one. This is the second-disagreement stop: if you still disagree, agreement=false and findings must name what a human must decide — the lane stop-rules this record, so make the open question crisp and short. Write {run.scratch}/rescore.json.

agreement.description: true iff the repaired body clears the rubric

nodes.goal: Apply exactly ONE disposition to record {run.item}. Read {run.scratch}/author.json, rubric.json, and (if present) repair.json, rescore.json. Decision rule, in order: author verdict=skip-not-mine -> skip-not-mine (no write). rubric agreement=true -> workable. rescore present with agreement=true -> workable. rescore present with agreement=false (second disagreement — the stop rule fired) -> needs-human. repair said repaired=false, or a finding names unclear intent -> needs-human. author split_campaign=true or a finding says 'split-campaign' -> needs-design. rubric finds the record should not exist -> reject-close (comment first, then close with the reason). Writes: set the disposition label on the record (skip for skip-not-mine) and leave one verdict-line comment: 'admission-lane: <disposition> — <one-line rationale>'. needs-human comments must open with 'needs-decision:' so the human-intake carrier can find them. Exactly one disposition — no hedging, no untouched record unless skip-not-mine. Write {run.scratch}/disposition.json.

applied.description: true iff the label+comment write succeeded

disposition.description: exactly one of: workable | needs-design | needs-human | reject-close | skip-not-mine
